sourcedFrom: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) (2018)
cleanIntro: The VSKA is Century Arms' US-made AK-pattern semi-auto in 7.62x39, and it strips the way every AK strips: dust cover, recoil spring, carrier and bolt, and that is the whole field strip. Century's own AK manual is written for the pattern rather than for one model, so read it with your own rifle in front of you — most importantly, it deliberately refuses to tell you what your rifle is chambered for and sends you to the caliber marking on the gun instead.

steps.title: The book will not tell you the chambering — the rifle will
steps.action: Before anything else, read the caliber designation marked on your rifle and match your ammunition to it exactly. Century writes this manual for AK-pattern rifles as a class and states plainly that they come in several calibers, so it deliberately declines to say what is in your chamber. On a 7.62x39 VSKA the near-misses are real: 7.62x39 and 5.45x39 magazines and rounds live in the same shape of rifle.
steps.prose: This is the manual bounding its own coverage, not a throwaway line. A category book cannot know which gun is in the box, so it hands that one decision back to you.
steps.quote: NOTICE: AK-style rifles are chambered in several calibers.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Cover, printed p.1
steps.warn: Confirm the ammunition you load into your firearm and magazines matches exactly with the caliber designation on your firearm.

steps.title: Safety up, magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and rotate the safety lever up to SAFE first, then take the magazine out. Hold the receiver with one hand, take your other hand off the grip and grasp the magazine, press the magazine release lever forward with your thumb, then rock the bottom of the magazine toward the muzzle and lift it clear of the well.
steps.prose: An AK magazine rocks out, it does not drop out. Trying to pull it straight down fights the front locking lug.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine from the rifle. With one hand holding the receiver, remove your other hand from the rifle grip and grasp the magazine. Using your thumb, depress the magazine release lever.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Unloading the Rifle, printed p.9
steps.warn: The rifle will fire if the magazine is removed and if the trigger is pulled when a cartridge is in the chamber.

steps.title: Chamber checked by eye, then the bolt goes home
steps.action: Drop the safety to FIRE so the bolt can travel, pull the cocking handle fully back and look into the chamber. Confirm with your eyes that it is empty and that no magazine is in the rifle, then let the bolt go forward and put the safety back up to SAFE.
steps.prose: The AK safety lever doubles as a bolt-travel stop, which is why it has to come down to check the chamber and goes straight back up afterwards.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber to ensure it is empty. Once you determine the chamber is empty and no magazine is in the rifle, let the bolt go forward.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Unloading the Rifle, printed p.9
steps.warn: WARNING! Always unload your rifle immediately after use and prior to cleaning and storage to minimize the risk of an accidental discharge.

steps.title: Eye protection on, and prove it empty again
steps.action: Put shooting glasses on before a single part moves — this strip releases a captive spring straight back toward your face. Then run the unload check again from the top: magazine out, safety to FIRE, chamber looked at, bolt forward, and every loaded magazine and live round off the bench.
steps.prose: Century asks for the unload sequence twice on purpose: once to unload, once to open. Never assume a rifle is unloaded because you were the one who put it down.
steps.quote: WARNING! Before beginning the disassembly process, check to ensure the rifle is not loaded.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Field Stripping, printed p.10
steps.warn: WARNING! Wear eye protection, such as shooting glasses or goggles, when disassembling your firearm to protect your eyes from tensioned parts, such as springs that could be dislodged during disassembly.

steps.title: Dust cover off — thumb on the recoil spring cam
steps.action: Brace the rifle in your lap or on a table with the muzzle safe. Press in on the recoil spring cam at the rear of the receiver with the thumb of your strong hand while lifting the dust cover with the other, and take the cover off rear end first. The cam is what holds the cover down; keep pressure on it until the cover is clear.
steps.prose: The cover comes off backwards, not upwards. Lift the front first and you are levering the cover's lip against the rear sight block.
steps.quote: With the rifle secured, use the thumb of your primary hand to press in on the recoil spring cam, while lifting the dust cover off the receiver with your support hand.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Field Stripping, step 4, printed p.10

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out — it is under load
steps.action: Hold the forward part of the receiver and press on the back of the recoil spring cam until its rear face clears the groove in the rear of the receiver, then lift the cam and draw the recoil spring assembly forward out of the bolt carrier channel. Keep a hand on it the whole way: it is compressed, and it will leave under its own power if you let go.
steps.prose: The tell that it is clear is the rear face lifting out of the groove. Until that happens you are pushing against the receiver, not the spring.
steps.aside: The stray "Illustration #11" inside that sentence is a figure callout that sits mid-line in the printed page.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the recoil spring assembly from the rifle by holding the forward Illustration #11 portion of the receiver with your hand and pressing on the back of the recoil spring cam with your other hand until its rear face leaves the groove in the rear of the receiver.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Field Stripping, step 5, printed p.10
steps.warn: NOTE: The recoil spring assembly is under spring pressure. Hold on to the assembly when removing it or injury could result.

steps.title: Carrier and bolt back and up
steps.action: Hold the receiver with one hand and the cocking handle with the other and draw the carrier and bolt fully to the rear. When the back of the carrier meets the receiver's backplate, lift the rear of the carrier and take it and the bolt up and out of the receiver.
steps.prose: There is a relief cut at the back of the rails that only lines up at full travel. If the carrier will not lift, it is not all the way back.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the bolt carrier and bolt from the rifle by holding the receiver with one hand and the cocking handle with your other hand. Pull the bolt carrier and bolt to the rear as far as possible.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Field Stripping, step 6, printed p.10

steps.title: Bolt out of the carrier — rotate, drop, rotate again
steps.action: Hold the carrier with the cocking handle to the left. Rotate the bolt counter-clockwise and let it drop to the bottom of the cam track, then keep rotating counter-clockwise until the bolt cam exits the track, and lift the bolt up and out.
steps.prose: It is one continuous motion, not two: the bolt has to be at the bottom of the track before the cam will clear it. Force it at the top and you are twisting against the carrier.
steps.quote: To remove the bolt from the bolt carrier, hold the bolt carrier in your primary hand so that the cocking handle faces to the left.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Field Stripping, step 7, printed p.10

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, brush then patch, until clean
steps.action: Fit the correct calibre brush to a cleaning rod, damp it with solvent and run it through the barrel several times. Swap to a correctly sized patch and push that through several times to carry the loosened fouling out. Alternate brush and patches until a patch comes out clean, then put a light film of oil in the bore.
steps.prose: Century's stopping condition is a clean patch, not a number of strokes. On a 7.62x39 rifle that usually takes more passes than people expect.
steps.quote: 6. Repeat this process with the brush and cleaning patches until a final patch comes out clean after swabbing the bore. Lightly oil the bore.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Cleaning the Rifle, printed p.12
steps.warn: WARNING! Excessive use of cleaning solvents or lubricants can adversely affect your rifle's functioning. Wipe the inside of the barrel dry before firing and ensure that it is free of obstructions.

steps.title: Action parts wiped, solvent removed, then oiled
steps.action: Wipe residue off the carrier, bolt, piston and the inside of the receiver with a soft cloth dabbed in solvent, then get every trace of that solvent back off and dry the parts. Only once they are dry does a light film of good gun oil go on the outer surfaces.
steps.prose: Solvent left in the receiver keeps working on the finish and creeps into the trigger group. Gloves are worth wearing — a stamped AK receiver has genuinely sharp edges inside.
steps.caution: WARNING! There may be sharp edges on parts of the firearm. Keep your fingers protected by wearing a pair of protective gloves when cleaning.
steps.quote: 7. Remove shooting residue from the rifle's action parts and outer surfaces by wiping them with a soft cloth dabbed in gun cleaning solvent. Be sure to remove all excess solvent and dry the parts.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Cleaning the Rifle, printed p.12

steps.title: How often, and why it is not just about shooting
steps.action: Clean it as soon as you can after firing. Century also asks for regular cleaning even when the rifle has not been fired at all, on a schedule set by where you live: once or twice a year in dry air, as often as weekly in humid air. In freezing weather a dry lubricant works better than oil.
steps.prose: Corrosion does not wait for a range trip. A safe queen in a damp house needs more attention than a range rifle in a dry one.
steps.quote: Always clean your rifle as soon as possible after firing to prevent buildup of shooting residue and to prevent corrosion from starting.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Cleaning Intervals, printed p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Dust cover, recoil spring assembly, bolt carrier and bolt are off the rifle and the bolt is out of the carrier. That is the whole field strip this manual publishes — the trigger group, gas block and barrel stay where they are, and Century's own instruction is that worn or damaged parts are a gunsmith's job.
steps.prose: If a case is still stuck in the chamber at this point, stop. The manual says an unstripped-out casing goes to a gunsmith rather than back into a reassembled rifle.
steps.quote: WARNING! This firearm should be checked periodically for worn or damaged parts by a competent gunsmith.
steps.cite: SEMI-AUTO RIFLE (AK STYLE) — ©2018 Century Arms. All Rights Reserved. (footer, all 15 pages) — Cleaning the Rifle, printed p.13

deepAbsentReason: Century Arms publishes no procedure deeper than the field strip above. The manual's disassembly content is exactly the Field Stripping section (printed p.10, seven steps ending with the bolt out of the carrier) and the Reassembly section (p.11); there is no trigger-group, gas-system, barrel or furniture procedure anywhere in its 15 pages, and its own instruction for anything further is that the rifle 'should be checked periodically for worn or damaged parts by a competent gunsmith' and that a case which cannot be extracted after a field strip goes to a gunsmith rather than back into a reassembled rifle. Century's manuals index publishes four PDFs in total and none of the other three is deeper. Nothing beyond what the book prints has been invented.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Correct-calibre brush on a rod, damped with solvent, several passes
Correctly sized patches until a patch comes out clean
Light oil in the bore afterwards
Wipe the bore DRY before firing and check it is free of obstructions

cleaning.name: BOLT, CARRIER & PISTON
tasks: Soft cloth dabbed in solvent over the carrier, bolt face, cam track and piston
Remove all excess solvent and dry the parts
Check the bolt rotates freely in the carrier cam track before reassembly
Gloves on — a stamped receiver and a bolt carrier both have sharp edges

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & OUTER SURFACES
tasks: Wipe residue from the receiver interior, rails and the gas tube block
Finish with a soft cloth dipped in good quality gun oil over all outer surfaces
Below freezing, use a dry lubricant instead of oil
Never spray or apply lubricant onto ammunition

cleaning.name: AFTER EVERY SESSION
tasks: Clean as soon as possible after firing
Clean on a schedule even when unfired — yearly in dry air, up to weekly in humid air
Wash hands and face afterwards; this is lead exposure
Store cleaned and lightly oiled, unloaded, locked and separate from ammunition

reassembly: Hold the carrier with the piston pointing up and the cocking handle to the left, drop the bolt into the large hole and let it fall to the bottom, then rotate it clockwise until the bolt cam enters the cam track; turn the carrier piston-down and the bolt runs forward to the open position.
Make sure the hammer is cocked and locked under the sear before the carrier goes anywhere near the receiver.
Point the muzzle at the ground, place the gas piston into the gas tube and slide the carrier forward until its guide grooves line up with the receiver rails.
Press down on the carrier so it slightly depresses the hammer, and let the bolt close fully.
Insert the recoil spring retainer into the bolt carrier channel and seat the recoil spring cam back into its groove in the rear of the receiver.
Fit the front edge of the receiver cover into the groove in the back of the gas tube block, lower the rear, and press the recoil spring cam through until it locks the cover down.
Function check the safety and the bolt travel, then check the bore is clear before the rifle is loaded.
fncheck: With the rifle unloaded and no magazine fitted, work the cocking handle fully and let the bolt run forward — it must close all the way with no drag and no ride-forward. Put the safety up to SAFE and confirm the lever blocks the cocking handle from being drawn back far enough to chamber a round and that the trigger will not release the hammer; drop it to FIRE and confirm normal function. Check the receiver cover is seated and the recoil spring cam is fully engaged in its groove, so the cover cannot lift under recoil. Finally look through the bore from the chamber end against a light and confirm it is clear and dry.
